Subject: Post-demo procurement checklist & payment path decision

Hi Ethan — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the procurement items I promised to send: 

1) High-level ask: please confirm which commercial path you prefer so we can route paperwork correctly — options are (a) Purchase Order (PO) invoicing to your AP, (b) Credit Card / P-Card, or (c) AWS Marketplace / Cloud marketplace billing.

2) If PO: we need the PO number and the billing contact. Standard terms are net-30; finance can review net-45 if you need that for enterprise deals.

3) If Card: we can invoice via our payments portal; no vendor setup required but card fees may apply depending on your card provider.

4) If Marketplace: there are advantages for consolidated billing, but it requires marketplace enablement and may add a 5% marketplace fee and longer provisioning for entitlements. Let us know if you need us to walk procurement through that flow.

5) Vendor intake forms: we need a completed W-9 (for US entities) or W-8BEN-E (for non-US), plus banking instructions if you want ACH/wire. If you prefer the vendor portal route, we can send an enrollment link — that often speeds up verification.

Next steps I propose: you confirm preferred payment route and either (a) attach W-9 + bank details to this thread or (b) tell me to send the vendor portal link and we’ll enroll you. Once we have the forms, finance will share a sample invoice and the expected timeline for first billing.

I’ve cc’d Marissa (commercial ops) who can help with onboarding and the vendor packet.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni

Hi Ethan — looping in details so procurement can move quickly. Short answers first, then links: 

- PO / Net terms: Yes, Redwood accepts POs. Our default is net-30; for enterprise customers we can approve net-45 on the contract (requires commercial sign-off). Vivek can escalate if you need net-45 in place before contract signature, but finance will usually accept a PO up front for provisioning.

- Marketplace: We do support AWS Marketplace and other cloud marketplaces. Marketplace billing simplifies line-of-business chargebacks but adds a marketplace fee (typically ~5%) and may delay entitlement mapping by 3–5 business days while marketplace entitlements are synchronized. If you need rapid provisioning and no marketplace fees, PO/direct invoicing tends to be faster.

- Bank template / ACH: Preferred is our banking spreadsheet (sample attached link) or a bank letter. Required fields: company legal name, EIN, bank name, routing number, account number, account type, and an authorized signer. If you attach an XLSX with those fields we can push it straight to finance for verification.

Links / attachments: Vendor portal enrollment (optional): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_vendor_onboarding_template
Sample vendor spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1b2C_sample_bank_template/view

Next steps: 1) Tell us preferred payment path (PO vs card vs marketplace). 2) If PO — send W-9 + bank form and the AP contact and we’ll confirm timeline and any contract term adjustments. 3) If marketplace — confirm and we’ll start the enablement flow.

If you want, I can send a short vendor packet PDF (instructions + sample invoice) to procurement to make the process straightforward.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
